```{r setup}
library(pmxvpc)
```

A Visual Predictive Check (VPC) compares percentiles of observed
concentration-time data against the corresponding percentiles from
simulated replicates of the same design, as a diagnostic for whether a
pharmacometric model reproduces the variability seen in real data.
`pmxvpc` builds VPC plots and summary tables from simulated and
observed datasets, with optional stratification, time binning, and
prediction/variance correction (pcVPC/pvcVPC).

This vignette walks through the full pipeline using the small
synthetic datasets shipped with the package, `pmxvpc_sim_example` (20
simulated replicates for 8 subjects at two dose levels) and
`pmxvpc_obs_example` (one observed realization per subject).

```{r}
head(pmxvpc_sim_example)
head(pmxvpc_obs_example)
```

## 1. Load and prepare the data

`load_vpc_data()` maps each dataset's columns to the structure the rest
of the package expects, and identifies which columns are common to
both datasets (and therefore usable for stratification).

```{r}
data <- load_vpc_data(
  sim_data = pmxvpc_sim_example,
  obs_data = pmxvpc_obs_example,
  sim_time = "TIME",
  sim_endpoint = "DV",
  obs_time = "TIME",
  obs_endpoint = "DV",
  sim_repl = "REP",
  sim_subject = "ID",
  obs_subject = "ID",
  nominal_times = c(0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 24)
)

data$available_strata
```

## 2. Configure stratification

`configure_strata()` chooses which of those common variables to split
plots and tables by, and optionally maps numeric codes to display
labels.

```{r}
strata <- configure_strata(
  data,
  eligible_vars = "DOSE",
  manual_labels = list(DOSE = "100 = Low dose\n300 = High dose")
)
```

## 3. Choose plot settings

`vpc_plot_settings()` validates and collects the options that control
how the plots look and whether a prediction/variance correction is
applied.

```{r}
settings <- vpc_plot_settings(
  strat_vars = "DOSE",
  log_scale = TRUE
)
```

## 4. Generate the plots

```{r}
plots <- plot_vpc_strata(data, settings)
plots$plots[["DOSE=100"]]
```

### Combining stratified plots

`combine_vpc_plots()` arranges every stratum panel into one image,
with a single shared legend.

```{r}
combine_vpc_plots(plots)
```

## 5. Summary tables

`summarise_vpc_data()` gives a per-stratum overview (record counts,
descriptive statistics); `summarise_vpc_percentiles()` gives the
simulated and observed percentiles underlying the plot, by stratum and
time bin.

```{r}
summarise_vpc_data(data, strat_vars = "DOSE")
summarise_vpc_percentiles(data, strat_vars = "DOSE")
```

## Prediction- and variance-corrected VPCs

When subjects differ in dose (or other covariates), a plain VPC isn't
always comparable across a bin. Setting `correction = "pc"` rescales
each record to the bin's typical prediction first; `correction = "pvc"`
additionally corrects for variability differences between simulated
replicates. Both require a prediction column (`sim_pred`/`obs_pred`);
`"pvc"` also requires the simulated replicate column already mapped
above (`sim_repl`).

```{r}
data_pred <- load_vpc_data(
  sim_data = pmxvpc_sim_example,
  obs_data = pmxvpc_obs_example,
  sim_time = "TIME",
  sim_endpoint = "DV",
  obs_time = "TIME",
  obs_endpoint = "DV",
  sim_repl = "REP",
  sim_subject = "ID",
  obs_subject = "ID",
  sim_pred = "PRED",
  obs_pred = "PRED",
  nominal_times = c(0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 24)
)

settings_pvc <- vpc_plot_settings(strat_vars = "DOSE", correction = "pvc")
plots_pvc <- plot_vpc_strata(data_pred, settings_pvc)
plots_pvc$plots[["DOSE=100"]]
```

See `?vpc_plot_settings` for the full rationale behind `"pc"` and
`"pvc"`, and Bergstrand et al. (2011)
[doi:10.1208/s12248-011-9255-z](https://doi.org/10.1208/s12248-011-9255-z)
for the original method.

## All-in-one: `run_vpc_analysis()`

For a single call that chains every step above (and optionally writes
plots/tables to disk via `*_save_path` arguments), use
`run_vpc_analysis()`:

```{r}
result <- run_vpc_analysis(
  sim_data = pmxvpc_sim_example,
  obs_data = pmxvpc_obs_example,
  sim_time = "TIME",
  sim_endpoint = "DV",
  obs_time = "TIME",
  obs_endpoint = "DV",
  sim_repl = "REP",
  sim_subject = "ID",
  obs_subject = "ID",
  nominal_times = c(0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 24),
  strat_vars = "DOSE"
)

result$overview
```
